subproblems.title: The open unit cube in Euclid k has volume 1
subproblems.statement: For every k ∈ ℕ, the open unit cube Q₁^k = {y ∈ Euclid k : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i : Fin k} has Lebesgue measure 1. Here Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with its standard volume, and y_i is the i-th coordinate of y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ k : ℕ, volume {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof. This is the fact vol(Q₁^k) = 1 that Simon uses as Lⁿ(F̆) = 1 in Ch. 6 §5, display (31).

Notation. For y : Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), y i means the i-th coordinate (ofLp y) i. Here ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ) is the canonical identification. Q₁^k := {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}.

1. Fix k ∈ ℕ. The map ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ) is measure preserving, from volume on Euclid k to the product Lebesgue measure volume on Fin k → ℝ (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp).
2. Let B := Set.pi univ (fun _ : Fin k => Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) = {f : Fin k → ℝ | ∀ i, 0 < f i < 1}. For y : Euclid k, y ∈ Q₁^k ⇔ ∀ i, 0 < (ofLp y) i < 1 ⇔ ofLp y ∈ B. Hence Q₁^k = ofLp⁻¹(B).
3. B is a finite product of the measurable open intervals Ioo 0 1, so it is measurable (MeasurableSet.univ_pi with measurableSet_Ioo). Under a measure-preserving map, the preimage of a measurable set has the same measure as the set (MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage). Therefore volume(Q₁^k) = volume(ofLp⁻¹(B)) = volume(B).
4. By the volume formula for open boxes (Real.volume_pi_Ioo), volume(B) = ∏_{i : Fin k} ENNReal.ofReal(1 − 0) = ∏_{i : Fin k} 1 = 1. For k = 0 the product is empty and again equals 1.
5. Steps 3 and 4 give volume(Q₁^k) = 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Q₁^k is the preimage of the box Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1) under ofLp : Euclid k → (Fin k → ℝ), which is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp).
The box is measurable, so its preimage has the same volume (MeasurePreserving.measure_preimage).
Real.volume_pi_Ioo gives volume(box) = ∏ ofReal(1 − 0) = 1. For k = 0 this is the empty product.

subproblems.title: Coordinates of the lattice face map b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)}
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let ι : Fin k → Fin P be injective, let b : Fin P → ℤ and let y ∈ Euclid k. Put e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ Euclid P and Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_{j : Fin k} y_j • e_{ι(j)} ∈ Euclid P, where toLp(b) is the vector with coordinates (b_i : ℝ). Then (i) Φ(y)_{ι(m)} = b_{ι(m)} + y_m for every m : Fin k, and (ii) Φ(y)_l = b_l for every l : Fin P with ι(m) ≠ l for all m : Fin k.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (ι : Fin k → Fin P) (b : Fin P → ℤ) (y : Euclid k), Function.Injective ι → (∀ m, (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (ι m) = (b (ι m) : ℝ) + y m) ∧ (∀ l, (∀ m, ι m ≠ l) → (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) l = (b l : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ) ∈ Euclid P. toLp(b) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) ∈ Euclid P. Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_{j : Fin k} y_j • e_{ι(j)}. For v ∈ Euclid P, v_l (written v l in Lean, i.e. ofLp v l) is the l-th coordinate.

1. Coordinates in Euclid P are additive and ℝ-linear: (u + v)_l = u_l + v_l and (c • v)_l = c · v_l. Also (Σ_j v_j)_l = Σ_j (v_j)_l (WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply). Moreover toLp(b)_l = (b_l : ℝ). Since e_i = toLp(Pi.single i 1), (e_i)_l = 1 if l = i and (e_i)_l = 0 otherwise (Pi.single_apply).
2. Hence for every l : Fin P, Φ(y)_l = b_l + Σ_{j : Fin k} y_j · (e_{ι(j)})_l = b_l + Σ_{j : Fin k} (if ι(j) = l then y_j else 0).
3. Proof of (i). Fix m : Fin k and take l = ι(m) in step 2. For j ≠ m, injectivity of ι gives ι(j) ≠ ι(m), so the j-th summand is 0. The m-th summand is y_m. Hence the sum equals y_m (Finset.sum_eq_single), and Φ(y)_{ι(m)} = b_{ι(m)} + y_m.
4. Proof of (ii). Fix l : Fin P with ι(m) ≠ l for all m : Fin k. Then every summand in step 2 is 0, so the sum is 0 and Φ(y)_l = b_l. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coordinates are additive and linear. toLp(b)_l = b_l, and (e_i)_l = 1 if l = i, else 0.
Hence Φ(y)_l = b_l + Σ_j (if ι(j) = l then y_j else 0).
At l = ι(m), injectivity of ι makes every summand except j = m vanish (Finset.sum_eq_single), giving b_{ι(m)} + y_m.
For l outside the range of ι every summand vanishes, giving b_l.

subproblems.title: The lattice face map is an isometry, with diameter at most √P on the closed unit cube
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let ι : Fin k → Fin P be injective, let b : Fin P → ℤ, and let Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_{j : Fin k} y_j • e_{ι(j)} (Euclid k → Euclid P), where e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and toLp(b) has coordinates (b_i : ℝ). Then (a) dist(Φ(y), Φ(y')) = dist(y, y') for all y, y' ∈ Euclid k; and (b) if 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y'_i ≤ 1 for all i, then dist(Φ(y), Φ(y')) ≤ √P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (ι : Fin k → Fin P) (b : Fin P → ℤ), Function.Injective ι → (∀ y y' : Euclid k, dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) = dist y y') ∧ (∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) ≤ Real.sqrt P)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 and 4 of the parent proof. Uses the sibling result face_coord (Submission.cmcdtfrfg_face_coord).

1. In Euclid n (n = k or n = P), dist(u, v) = √(Σ_i dist(u_i, v_i)²), and dist(s, t) = |s − t| on ℝ (EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, Real.dist_eq).
2. Fix P, k, an injective ι and b. Let y, y' ∈ Euclid k, x := Φ(y) and x' := Φ(y'). Apply face_coord to (ι, b, y) and to (ι, b, y'). For every m : Fin k, x_{ι(m)} = b_{ι(m)} + y_m and x'_{ι(m)} = b_{ι(m)} + y'_m. For every l : Fin P with ι(m) ≠ l for all m, x_l = b_l = x'_l.
3. Put g(l) := dist(x_l, x'_l)² for l : Fin P and f(m) := dist(y_m, y'_m)² for m : Fin k. By step 2, g(l) = |b_l − b_l|² = 0 for l outside the range of ι, and g(ι(m)) = |(b_{ι(m)} + y_m) − (b_{ι(m)} + y'_m)|² = |y_m − y'_m|² = f(m).
4. Since ι is injective and g vanishes outside range ι, Σ_{l : Fin P} g(l) = Σ_{m : Fin k} g(ι(m)) = Σ_m f(m) (Fintype.sum_of_injective). Explicitly: split the sum over l into range ι and its complement. The complement contributes 0. ι : Fin k → range ι is a bijection, so the part over range ι reindexes to Σ_m g(ι(m)).
5. By step 1, dist(x, x') = √(Σ_l g(l)) = √(Σ_m f(m)) = dist(y, y'). This proves (a).
6. For (b), assume 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y'_i ≤ 1 for all i. Then −1 ≤ y_m − y'_m ≤ 1, so f(m) = |y_m − y'_m|² ≤ 1 for each m. Hence Σ_m f(m) ≤ Σ_{m : Fin k} 1 = k, and since √ is monotone, dist(y, y') = √(Σ_m f(m)) ≤ √k.
7. Since ι : Fin k → Fin P is injective, k = card(Fin k) ≤ card(Fin P) = P (Fintype.card_le_of_injective). Hence √k ≤ √P.
8. By (a) and steps 6–7, dist(Φ(y), Φ(y')) = dist(y, y') ≤ √k ≤ √P. This proves (b). ∎
proof_key_steps: Euclidean distance is the square root of the sum of squared coordinate differences (EuclideanSpace.dist_eq).
By face_coord, the squared coordinate gaps of Φ(y) and Φ(y') vanish outside range ι and equal (y_m − y'_m)² at ι(m).
Reindexing the sum over Fin P along the injective ι (Fintype.sum_of_injective) gives dist(Φ y, Φ y') = dist(y, y').
On [0,1]^k each squared gap is ≤ 1, so dist(y, y') ≤ √k. Injectivity gives k ≤ P, hence the bound √P.

subproblems.title: Separation of distinct unit lattice faces
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let p = (ι, b), q = (ι', b') ∈ (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) with ι and ι' strictly increasing and p ≠ q. Let y ∈ Euclid k with 0 < y_j < 1 for all j, and y' ∈ Euclid k with 0 ≤ y'_i ≤ 1 for all i. Put x := Φ_p(y) = toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} and z := Φ_q(y') = toLp(b') + Σ_j y'_j • e_{ι'(j)}, where e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and toLp(b) has coordinates (b_i : ℝ). Then 1 ≤ dist(x, z), or there is j : Fin k with min(y_j, 1 − y_j) ≤ dist(x, z).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (p q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ)), StrictMono p.1 → StrictMono q.1 → p ≠ q → ∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → 1 ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∨ ∃ j, min (y j) (1 - y j) ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–8 of the parent proof. Uses the sibling result face_coord (Submission.cmcdtfrfg_face_coord).

1. Set-up. Write p = (ι, b) and q = (ι', b'). Strictly increasing maps are injective, so face_coord applies to (ι, b, y) and to (ι', b', y'). This gives:
 - x_{ι(m)} = b_{ι(m)} + y_m for all m : Fin k;
 - x_l = b_l whenever ι(m) ≠ l for all m;
 - z_{ι'(m)} = b'_{ι'(m)} + y'_m for all m;
 - z_l = b'_l whenever ι'(m) ≠ l for all m.
2. Coordinate bound. For every l : Fin P, |x_l − z_l| ≤ dist(x, z). Indeed dist(x, z)² = Σ_i (x_i − z_i)² ≥ (x_l − z_l)² (PiLp.dist_apply_le with Real.dist_eq).
3. Case A: there is j : Fin k such that NOT (b_{ι(j)} < z_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1). Write β := b_{ι(j)} ∈ ℤ and t := z_{ι(j)}. By step 1, x_{ι(j)} = β + y_j with 0 < y_j < 1.
 (a) If t ≤ β, then x_{ι(j)} − t ≥ y_j ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j).
 (b) Otherwise t ≥ β + 1, and t − x_{ι(j)} ≥ 1 − y_j ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j).
 In both cases |x_{ι(j)} − z_{ι(j)}| ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j). By step 2, min(y_j, 1 − y_j) ≤ dist(x, z), so the second alternative holds with this j.
4. Case B: b_{ι(j)} < z_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1 for every j : Fin k. In particular no z_{ι(j)} is an integer, because no integer lies strictly between the consecutive integers b_{ι(j)} and b_{ι(j)} + 1.
5. Case B, range inclusion: for every j, ι(j) = ι'(m) for some m. Otherwise ι'(m) ≠ ι(j) for all m, and step 1 gives z_{ι(j)} = b'_{ι(j)} ∈ ℤ. This contradicts step 4.
6. Case B, ι = ι'. Let S := {ι'(m) : m ∈ Fin k} ⊆ Fin P. Since ι' is injective, S has exactly k elements, and by step 5 both ι and ι' map Fin k into S. Let f : Fin k → Fin P be any strictly increasing map with values in S. Then f is injective, so its image is a k-element subset of the k-element set S, hence equals S. Thus f is a strictly increasing bijection Fin k → S. For each j, an element f(i) of S is smaller than f(j) iff i < j, by strict monotonicity and totality of the order on Fin k. So exactly j elements of S are smaller than f(j), and f(j) is the (j+1)-st smallest element of S. Applying this to f = ι and f = ι' shows that ι(j) and ι'(j) are both the (j+1)-st smallest element of S for every j, so ι = ι'. (In Mathlib both maps equal S.orderEmbOfFin by Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique. Equivalently, the ranges are equal and StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT applies.)
7. Case B, b and b' agree on range ι. Fix j. By step 1 for q (now ι' = ι), z_{ι(j)} = b'_{ι(j)} + y'_j ∈ [b'_{ι(j)}, b'_{ι(j)} + 1], since 0 ≤ y'_j ≤ 1. By step 4, z_{ι(j)} is not an integer, so b'_{ι(j)} < z_{ι(j)} < b'_{ι(j)} + 1 and hence b'_{ι(j)} = ⌊z_{ι(j)}⌋. Likewise b_{ι(j)} < z_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1 (step 4) gives b_{ι(j)} = ⌊z_{ι(j)}⌋. Hence b_{ι(j)} = b'_{ι(j)}. (Equivalently, in ℤ: b_{ι(j)} < b'_{ι(j)} + 1 and b'_{ι(j)} < b_{ι(j)} + 1.)
8. Case B, conclusion. We have p = (ι, b) ≠ q = (ι, b') with equal first components, so b ≠ b' and there is l : Fin P with b_l ≠ b'_l. By step 7, ι(m) ≠ l for all m, so l lies outside the range of ι = ι'. By step 1, x_l = b_l and z_l = b'_l. Since b_l − b'_l is a nonzero integer, |x_l − z_l| = |b_l − b'_l| ≥ 1. By step 2, 1 ≤ dist(x, z), so the first alternative holds.
9. Cases A and B are exhaustive, which proves the claim. For k = 0, Case A cannot occur because there is no j. Case B then applies: ι = ι' is the empty map, every l lies outside its range, and step 8 gives 1 ≤ dist(x, z). ∎
proof_key_steps: face_coord gives the coordinates of x = Φ_p(y) and z = Φ_q(y'), and each coordinate gap |x_l − z_l| is at most dist(x, z).
Case A: some z_{ι(j)} lies outside (b_{ι(j)}, b_{ι(j)} + 1). Since x_{ι(j)} = b_{ι(j)} + y_j, the gap at ι(j) is at least min(y_j, 1 − y_j).
Case B: every z_{ι(j)} is a non-integer in (b_{ι(j)}, b_{ι(j)} + 1). So range ι ⊆ range ι', and ι = ι' because both are strictly increasing enumerations of the same k-element set.
Then b' = b on range ι by the floor argument. Since p ≠ q, some l outside range ι has b_l ≠ b'_l, where x_l = b_l and z_l = b'_l differ by at least 1.
